newsitem.title: UKRAINE: No direct credits from Ukraine c.bank in '97 - head.
newsitem.headline: No direct credits from Ukraine c.bank in '97 - head.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank chairman Viktor Yushchenko said on Wednesday the bank would not issue direct credits to the government for deficit financing this year, despite parliament's attempts to ensure such credits.

"The firm position of the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU), in agreement with the Ministry of Finance, is that 1997 will be the first year the country will not issue credits to cover the budget deficit," Viktor Yushchenko told reporters.

Parliament, debating the long-delayed 1997 budget draft in its second reading on Tuesday, rejected a proposal to use only funds from the Treasury bill market to cover 3.33 billion hryvnias of the projected 5.7 billion hryvnia deficit.

He said the bank and ministry were strongly lobbying parliament, scheduled to debate the budget in its third and final reading on Thursday, to vote against allowing the central bank to cover part of the deficit with direct credits.
Yushchenko said money raised from the sale of Treasury bills would cover the 3.33 billion hryvnias. Parliament also ruled to cover 2.4 billion hryvnias of the deficit from foreign credits.

"The leitmotif of the NBU's 1997 monetary policy is such that with marked development of our money market, with solid demand for our Treasury bills, to return to the medieval practice of issuing direct credits -- this inarguably threatens the stability of our currency," Yushchenko said.
The central bank chief also said the bank had not issued credits to the government this year, despite Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov's statements to parliament on Tuesday.
Yushchenko explained official data which said the bank issued 32.9 million hryvnias toward the deficit since the start of 1997 reflected fluctuations in the currency's level.
Passage of this year's budget is a key condition Ukraine must meet if it hopes to receive a long-term, multi-billion dollar credit from the International Monetary Fund.
